newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts extend gains in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts extend gains in U.S..

text.p: Emerging market debts rose across the board in moderate trade ahead of the U.S. elections.
The direction of U.S. Treasuries after the election on Tuesday would be crucial in determining if the uptrend could be sustained, traders said.
"Spreads have tightened," said Ingrid Iverson, Brady bond strategist at UBS Securities. "But it is vulnerable to the long bond."
Brazil papers that had lagged in last week's rally took the lead, with the Brazil C bond gaining 1-5/8 to bid 71-3/8.
Marcelo Fleury, head of Brazil desk at Garban Corp, said investors were getting over the nagging "supply" concerns.
The $750 million five-year global bond last week was poorly timed before the U.S. Treasuries rallied, he said.
Priced at 99-7/8, or 265 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries, the bond subsequently traded at over 300 basis points in the secondary market, spilling weakness to Brazil Bradies.
In the buoyancy of emerging market debt prices, Brazil looked underpriced and was belatedly catching up, Fleury said.
"If the bond were priced today, it would have been much tighter," he said, quoting the secondary market bid at par and offered 105.
Portfolio adjustments also boosted other laggards, such as Nigeria and the Philippines, traders said.
Nigeria Pars rose 2-7/8 yo 64 bid, and Philippine Pars added 1-3/8 to 85-1/4 bid.
For Argentina, a seven-year 200 million Swiss franc eurobond, with seven percnet coupon, was priced Monday at 102-1/4. The new supply did not affect the market, traders said.
"The non-dollar issues usually do not move the Bradies," Iverson said.
With this issue, Argentina met all its funding needs for this year, and,unless for opportunistic reasons, it would not flood the market with more supply this year, she said.
Russia debts rose across the board. President Boris Yeltsin appeared to be in good shape to undergo heart surgery on Tuesday, which was received by investors as good news, Iverson said.
Clarification of the frozen Minfin bonds, though the amount was larger than previously reported, helped investors to gain a better grasp of which tranches were frozen, she added.
Russia dollar-denominated Vnesh loans rose 1-5/8 to 75-1/2 bid. Min Fin 3 added 1/2 to 80 bid. -- Nailene Chou Wiest, 212-859-1674
